apology: Write a text message to a close friend apologising for missing their wedding last Saturday. I overslept after a night shift. Four sentences at most.
headline: Write the headline and first line of a local news post: the Fourth Street bridge closes for six months of repairs starting Monday.
error: Write the error message a user sees when their card payment fails because the bank declined it. They can try another card or retry.
toast: Write a one-minute toast to be spoken aloud at the retirement party of Dana, who ran the town library for thirty years and never once closed it for snow.
release-note: Write the release note for version 2.3.1 of a password manager: a bug that could log users out mid-session is fixed, and the autofill delay is gone.
game-turn: You are the narrator of a text game. The player typed: 'I pick the lock on the cellar door.' The cellar holds the innkeeper's stolen ledger and the innkeeper is asleep upstairs. Write the turn.
agent-reply: You are a coding agent reporting back. The test suite failed: 3 of 212 tests, all in the date parser, because the new timezone table has no entry for Nepal. Write the reply to the developer.
thread-opener: Write the first post of a thread on why most meetings should have been a document. Under 280 characters.
eulogy: Write one paragraph to be read at the burial of a cat named Ferris, who lived nineteen years and slept on the writer's chest every night of them.
insult: Write a single cutting line a duellist says to the man who just missed him from ten paces.
parallel-invited: Write a story of about 300 words. Forty years apart, two women each work their first night shift alone at the same bakery: Ruth, who is retiring this week and owns it now, and Mae, nineteen, whom Ruth has hired to take it over. Tonight is Mae's first night alone.
single-character: Write a scene of about 250 words: a man alone in his kitchen at two in the morning tries to fix a tap that will not stop dripping.
